Anya: Observed weird thrashing when small hedge deltas land. Proposal: 'escrowed apply' semantics - runtime fetches a patch, computes apply_plan, then requests a short-lived apply_token before switching.
Ravi: Escrow token sounds good. Token should be HMAC-signed and very short lived (30s). Runtimes without token enter conservative mode.
Sam: Conservative mode = last-known-active manifest for N minutes, then revert to safe defaults. We need to pick N (suggest 5m).
Tess: Also add merge_mode on patches: strict / additive-only / permissive. Default additive-only for canary.
Anya: Good. Add grace_window option so controllers can request a wait period (seconds) to drain in-flight requests.
Ravi: Edge-case: private deployments where controller time drifts. Allow runtimes to accept tokens if token signature verifies and token includes base_seq.
Sam: We should require mutual TLS for hosted control plane calls; for Private, tokens + aud claim. Document rotation strategy.
Tess: Telemetry: sampled decision upload with decision_id, manifest_seq, applied_patch_id, local_probe_ms, and whether token was used. Batch and cap per tenant.
Anya: Probe-hedge model: runtime may request a bounded probe-hedge (max_extra_ms, max_cost_delta). Controller can grant or deny; if granted it returns a probe_token.
Ravi: Implement plan: 1) RFC for escrow + merge modes + tokens 2) small token service + signer 3) runtime stale-grace logic 4) probe-hedge flow + telemetry 5) console timeline for patch history.
ops-bot: @deploybot scheduled canary: manifest-escrow-svc v0.1 -> staging. job=90110.
Anya: I'll write the RFC today, include defaults (stale_grace=5m, token_ttl=30s, probe_sample=0.5%). Comments by Friday please.
